title: 5.12 Ancient torus curves in higher codimension
search_title: Ancient torus curves in higher codimension
section: 5.12 Ancient torus curves in higher codimension
text: D28FAF32B556 (Compact ancient torus curves) Fix $m\geq 2$ and integers $1=k_1<k_2<\cdots <k_ m$. For $t<0$, let $r(t)>0$ be the unique solution of \[  \sum _{j=1}^ m r(t)^{2k_ j^2}=-2t.  \] Then the exact parametrization \[  \gamma _ t(\theta )= \bigl (r(t)^{k_1^2}\cos (k_1\theta ),r(t)^{k_1^2}\sin (k_1\theta ), \ldots ,r(t)^{k_ m^2}\cos (k_ m\theta ),r(t)^{k_ m^2}\sin (k_ m\theta )\bigr ), \qquad \theta \in \mathbb R/2\pi \mathbb Z,  \] is an ancient curve-shortening flow in $\mathbb R^{2m}$. Its scale is specified by an exact implicit equation; no elementary inverse in time is required. Equivalently, \[  r'=-\frac{r}{\sum _ j k_ j^2r^{2k_ j^2}}.  \] Each time slice is a compact smooth embedded circle, hence complete and proper, with no ends and codimension $2m-1$. Embeddedness follows directly from $k_1=1$, because the first two coordinates already determine $\theta $. The name refers to a curve lying on a product of circles, not to a two-dimensional torus. It spans $\mathbb R^{2m}$, has a one-parameter simultaneous rotational symmetry, and is non-self-similar when $m\geq 2$ because the ratios of its different coordinate radii change with time. The rescaled curves $(-t)^{-1/2}\gamma _ t$ tend to the radius-$\sqrt2$ circle with multiplicity $k_ m$ as $t\to -\infty $, and with multiplicity one as $t\uparrow 0$. Stryker–Sun prove \[  \sup _{t<0}\lambda (\gamma _ t)=k_ m\lambda (S^1) =k_ m\sqrt{\frac{2\pi }{e}},  \] which also bounds the entropy of every time slice. This is a supremum over time, not a formula for the entropy at each finite time. For the fixed center and Gaussian scale, direct integration gives \[  F_{0,1}(\gamma _ t)=\sqrt\pi \left(\sum _ j k_ j^2r^{2k_ j^2}\right)^{1/2}e^{t/2}.  \] Indeed, $|\gamma _ t|^2=-2t$ and $|\partial _\theta \gamma _ t|^2=\sum _ jk_ j^2r^{2k_ j^2}$. The centered Gaussian area is distinct from the supremum defining $\lambda $. Source: [ SS19 ] , equation (2.1), Propositions 2.1–2.2, Corollary 2.3, and Theorem A.1, PDF pp. 3–5 and 8–9. The general source formula allows $k_1>1$; if the frequencies have common divisor $d>1$, that parametrization is a $d$-fold cover and its mass counts multiplicity. The embedded subfamily above avoids this ambiguity. The construction was already present in [ AAAW13 ] , Section 3, equations (11)–(14), PDF pp. 8–9, as acknowledged in [ SS19 ] , Remark 1.3. The interactive figure uses $(k_1,k_2)=(1,2)$ in $\mathbb R^4$. Its three-coordinate display is a projection, with time and fourth-coordinate rotation controls. title: 5.6 Eternal shrinking helices
text: 1EF23C4EFFC0 (Helical curve-shortening flows) Fix $m\geq 1$ and integers $1\leq k_1<\cdots <k_ m$. Let $r(t)>0$, $t\in \mathbb R$, solve the exact implicit equation \[  \log r(t)+\frac12\sum _{j=1}^ m r(t)^{2k_ j^2}=\frac m2-t.  \] The choice of constant makes $r(0)=1$. Then \[  \Gamma _ t(s)= \bigl (r^{k_1^2}\cos (k_1s),r^{k_1^2}\sin (k_1s),\ldots , r^{k_ m^2}\cos (k_ ms),r^{k_ m^2}\sin (k_ ms),s\bigr ), \qquad s\in \mathbb R,  \] is an eternal curve-shortening flow in $\mathbb R^{2m+1}$. In the simplest case $m=1$, $k_1=1$, it is the three-dimensional helix \[  \Gamma _ t(s)=(r(t)\cos s,r(t)\sin s,s),\qquad \log r(t)+r(t)^2/2=1/2-t.  \] These are exact parametrizations with an implicitly determined time scale, not numerical ODE profiles. The ordinary differential equation is \[  r'=-\frac{r}{1+\sum _ j k_ j^2r^{2k_ j^2}}.  \] The last coordinate makes every time slice a proper embedding of $\mathbb R$, and the induced metric is $(1+\sum _ jk_ j^2r^{2k_ j^2})ds^2$, so it is complete. It is noncompact with two ends and codimension $2m$, and it spans the stated ambient space. Simultaneous rotations together with translation along the last coordinate give its screw symmetry. Its radius decreases to zero as $t\to +\infty $, giving local smooth convergence to the axis, while $r(t)\to \infty $ as $t\to -\infty $. At any fixed finite time the ends continue winding; they are not asymptotic to the axis as $|s|\to \infty $. Proposition 2.7 of [ SS19 ] proves \[  \sup _{t\in \mathbb R}\lambda (\Gamma _ t)=+\infty .  \] This concerns the entire time family and does not say that every individual slice has infinite entropy. In fact, a direct calculation gives the exact fixed-time entropy below. Set $B=\sum _ jr^{2k_ j^2}$ and $D=\sum _ jk_ j^2r^{2k_ j^2}$. Direct Gaussian integration, using $|\Gamma _ t(s)|^2=B+s^2$, gives the exact centered value \[  F_{0,1}(\Gamma _ t)=\sqrt{1+D}\, e^{-B/4}; \qquad F_{0,1}(\Gamma _ t)=\sqrt{1+r^2}\, e^{-r^2/4} \quad \hbox{when }m=k_1=1.  \] For completeness, the same calculation at arbitrary Gaussian scale gives \[  \lambda (\Gamma _ t)=\sqrt{1+D(t)}.  \] Indeed, for a center $(a,z_0)\in \mathbb R^{2m}\times \mathbb R$, dropping the nonnegative squared distance in the first $2m$ coordinates bounds $F_{(a,z_0),\tau }$ by $(4\pi \tau )^{-1/2}\sqrt{1+D}\int _{\mathbb R}e^{-(s-z_0)^2/(4\tau )}\, ds=\sqrt{1+D}$. At the origin, $F_{0,\tau }=\sqrt{1+D}e^{-B/(4\tau )}$ tends to this upper bound as $\tau \to \infty $. Thus every finite-time helix has finite entropy, while the time supremum is infinite. This is a direct integration, additional to the cited time-supremum result. Source: [ SS19 ] , equation (2.6), Propositions 2.6–2.7, and Theorem A.2, PDF pp. 6–7 and 9; see also [ AAAW13 ] , Section 3, PDF pp. 8–10. The interactive three-dimensional figure uses the simplest exact helix, with a time slider and the displayed range $-5\pi /2\leq s\leq 5\pi /2$. title: 5.7 Immortal annuli converging to a double plane
search_title: Immortal annuli converging to a double plane
section: 5.7 Immortal annuli converging to a double plane
text: A50018836027 (Chen–Sun's noncompact multiplicity-two limit) Chen and Sun construct a nonstatic immortal mean curvature flow $M_ t\subset \mathbb R^3$, $t\in [0,\infty )$, smooth for $t>0$, of connected embedded rotational surfaces. It is also symmetric across the limiting plane. Each positive-time slice consists of two increasing radial graphs joined smoothly at a neck of radius $a(t)>0$: \[  M_ t=\{ (\rho \cos \theta ,\rho \sin \theta ,\pm f(\rho ,t)): \rho \geq a(t),\  \theta \in \mathbb R/2\pi \mathbb Z\} .  \] This is a description of the constructed PDE solution, not an explicit formula for $f$. Away from the neck its upper graph satisfies \[  f_ t=\frac{f_{\rho \rho }}{1+f_\rho ^2}+\frac{f_\rho }{\rho }.  \] Near the neck, the inverse graph $\rho =u(z,t)$ instead satisfies \[  u_ t=\frac{u_{zz}}{1+u_ z^2}-\frac1u,\qquad u_ z(0,t)=0.  \] The proof selects a critical initial surface by interpolation among rotational surfaces in finite cylinders and then takes a limit as the cylinder radius tends to infinity. Its initial trace is locally Lipschitz; choosing any positive time as the initial time gives an entirely smooth immortal flow. No closed formula, canonical parameter value, or uniqueness of the constructed critical flow is supplied. The two graphical ends and the smooth connecting neck give topology $S^1\times \mathbb R$: genus zero and two ends. Properness follows from the graphs escaping to infinite radius; the smooth connected surface is complete. It remains in a fixed slab, and the two ends stay asymptotic to their original parallel planes. The neck radius tends to zero only as $t\to \infty $. On compact regions the flow converges to the middle plane with multiplicity two; the two sheets converge smoothly away from the origin. The convergence is not uniform over the entire noncompact surface. This is an infinite-time limit of the unrescaled flow, not a multiplicity-two finite-time tangent flow of a closed embedded surface. Source: [ CS26R3 ] , Theorems 1.1 and 4.13, Section 1.1, equation (2.5), Proposition 4.6 and Remark 4.7, and Appendix A, arXiv v3 PDF pp. 1, 3, 6, 23–24, and 27–28. The topology and properness statements above are direct consequences of the source's two-graph parametrization. The paper gives no exact entropy or fixed-center Gaussian-area value for this constructed family. The interactive picture compares ordered finite-time stages and a separate infinite-time limit at a fixed viewing scale. A cutaway exposes the connecting neck; the compressed radial profile records the fixed far-end heights. text: 225751B3C7E8 (Chen–Sun's product-manifold construction) For each $n\geq 2$, there is a smooth connected embedded immortal mean curvature flow of compact hypersurfaces in the product manifold \[  (S^ n\times [-1,1],\  g_{S^ n}+dy^2),  \] where $S^ n$ has unit round radius. The flow is defined for all $t\geq 0$ and is nonstatic. Its hypersurface dimension is $n$ and its codimension in this ambient manifold is one. The construction stays in the smaller band $|y|\leq 1/(2n)$, so the same flow is contained in $S^ n\times \mathbb R$; it can also be placed in the closed product $S^ n\times (\mathbb R/4\mathbb Z)$ without changing the metric near the flow. There is no free boundary on $y=\pm 1$. The solution is invariant under rotations of the sphere about its polar axis, reflection $y\mapsto -y$, and reflection across the sphere's equator. A closed profile $\sigma \mapsto (x(\sigma ,t),y(\sigma ,t))$ in $(0,\pi )\times \mathbb R$ generates it by \[  (\sigma ,\omega )\longmapsto (\cos x(\sigma ,t),\sin x(\sigma ,t)\, \omega ,y(\sigma ,t)), \qquad \sigma \in S^1,\quad \omega \in S^{n-1}.  \] The profile avoids both axes at every finite time, so this parametrization directly gives topology $S^1\times S^{n-1}$. Thus for $n=2$ the surfaces are genus-one tori with no ends. All slices are complete and proper by compactness. This is a topological deduction from the construction, not an assertion that the source states a separate topology theorem. No closed time-dependent profile is supplied. Its upper half can be described using the solution of \[  v_ t=\frac{v_{xx}}{1+v_ x^2}+(n-1)\cot x\, v_ x, \qquad v_ x(\pi /2,t)=0,  \] with an inverse graph near each neck, governed by \[  u_ t=\frac{u_{yy}}{1+u_ y^2}-(n-1)\cot u, \qquad u_ y(0,t)=0.  \] An interpolation argument selects an immortal solution. As $t\to \infty $, it converges to the stable minimal slice $S^ n\times \{ 0\} $ with multiplicity two. Away from the north and south poles, the two sheets converge smoothly; the two necks collapse only at infinite time. Source: [ CS25Man ] , Theorems 1.1, 3.12, and 3.17, Section 2.1, Definition 3.10 and Lemma 3.11, and Section 3.3, arXiv v2 PDF pp. 1–4 and 11–15. Euclidean Gaussian area and Colding–Minicozzi entropy are not assigned to this intrinsic manifold flow; the cited paper gives no such invariant for these examples. In particular, its isometric embedding into $\mathbb R^{n+2}$ is not an unforced Euclidean mean curvature flow. The picture pairs three ordered finite-time stages with the infinite-time limit and their orbit-space profiles. In the $n=2$ drawing, the coordinate map $(p,y)\mapsto (1+2y)p$, for $p\in S^2$, displays the two sheets as inner and outer shells joined through both polar necks. This map is not an isometry: the radial separation illustrates the product coordinate, not a Euclidean MCF. title: 5.8 Haslhofer–Hershkovits ancient ovals
text: 56D296501918 For $n\geq 2$ and every $1\leq j\leq n-1$, Haslhofer–Hershkovits construct an ancient hypersurface flow $M_ t\subset \mathbb R^{n+1}$, $-\infty <t<0$, with compact strictly convex embedded slices. Each slice is diffeomorphic to $S^ n$, hence complete and proper with no ends. The construction has $O(j+1)\times O(n-j)$ symmetry and is uniformly Andrews noncollapsed. It is not self-similar and becomes round at extinction. Under backward parabolic blow-down, \[  \lambda ^{-1}M_{\lambda ^2t}\longrightarrow S^ j(\sqrt{2j|t|})\times \mathbb R^{n-j}\quad (\lambda \to \infty ).  \] The tip rescalings selected in Claim 3.5 of [ HH13 ] approach $\mathrm{Bowl}^{j+1}\times \mathbb R^{n-j-1}$, with the bowl normalized to unit tip curvature. Rescaled diameter is unbounded backward in time and curvature decay is type II. No closed formula or uniqueness follows from this construction. Gaussian area and entropy are finite for each compact slice; no fixed slice value is evaluated here. Source: [ HH13 ] , Theorem 1.1 and Section 3. Huisken–Sinestrari's Theorem 3.2 in [ HS14 ] shows why the hypothesis $h_{ij}\geq \varepsilon H g_{ij}$ with one $\varepsilon >0$ for all ancient times cannot hold for these nonspherical ovals: a closed convex ancient flow with that uniform pinching is a shrinking sphere. The illustration specializes to $n=2$, $j=1$. It numerically evolves the boundary of the Minkowski sum of a unit ball and an ellipsoid with semiaxes $(8,1/2,1/2)$, using rotational mean curvature flow. This is a finite smooth convex seed inspired by the long capped cylinders in Section 3, not a closed formula for the ancient oval. Extinction is shifted to $t=0$, and parabolic scaling makes the axial-to-equatorial radius ratio equal to $2$ at $t=-1$. The slider samples $-1000\leq t\leq -0.001$. Original size shows contraction at a fixed spatial scale. The default view shows $(-t)^{-1/2}M_ t$: the backward central limit is the cylinder of radius $\sqrt2$, while the extinction limit is the sphere of radius $2$. The right-tip view instead translates the tip to the origin and multiplies lengths by its mean curvature; the dashed comparison is a numerically integrated unit-speed bowl. These are different rescalings. title: 5.10 The eternal reapernoid
text: 8EACFCA7AE0F For every $n\geq 2$, Mramor–Payne construct an eternal embedded hypersurface flow $M_ t\subset \mathbb R^{n+1}$, $t\in \mathbb R$, on the outside of a rotational minimal catenoid. It is $O(n)\times O(1)$ invariant, mean convex with the chosen outward normal, nonconvex, and has uniformly bounded curvature. Backward in time it converges smoothly and uniformly to that catenoid; forward in time its distance from the rotation axis tends to infinity. It is not a translator or another soliton. The rotational graphical construction gives complete proper noncompact slices with topology $S^{n-1}\times \mathbb R$ and two ends. For $n=2$ these are annuli in $\mathbb R^3$. In that dimension the pointed forward profile limit is a line and curvature tends to zero. For $n\geq 3$, recentered meridians converge instead to a grim reaper with the same width as the higher-dimensional catenoid. These are pointed profile limits, not a claim that the unshifted surfaces converge globally to a fixed grim cylinder. Source: [ MP19 ] , Theorem 1.3, pp. 4–5, and Section 4. title: 5.2 Compact nonconvex ancient spiral curves

They are smooth simple closed curves, hence complete and proper, with no ends. They are nonconvex in the ancient regime and are neither shrinking circles nor ancient paperclips. No assertion of nonconvexity through a later maximal continuation is needed here. The limiting rotating model has angular speed one. Its radial expansion $\mathcal R(\theta )=\sqrt{2\theta }+O(\theta ^{-3/2})$ is asymptotic, not a formula for the constructed ancient curve. If $\Omega (t)$ is the paper's truncated spiral region and $\Lambda (t)$ is the enclosed ancient region, the Main Theorem proves \[  |\Lambda (t)\mathbin {\triangle }\Omega (t)|\leq C_\delta |t|^{-1+\delta }\qquad (t\to -\infty )  \] for each $\delta >0$. This is an area estimate, not an exact pointwise parametrization. Gaussian area and entropy are finite at each compact slice; no uniform ancient bound is assigned. Source: [ ZOKA23 ] , Main Theorem and equations (1.1)–(1.3), pp. 1–3, and Appendix A. No uniqueness is claimed. The source also credits Charyyev's independent construction. At a fixed point of the unrotated model the arms rotate counterclockwise with speed one. The cap center instead follows $R(t)E(-t)$, where $R(t)=\mathcal R(-2t)\sim 2\sqrt{-t}$, so it moves clockwise and inward. Its leading width is $\pi /R(t)$. To read the motion, write $E(\theta )=(\cos \theta ,\sin \theta )$ and $J(x,y)=(-y,x)$. The two arms are \[  Y_\pm (\theta ,t)=\mathcal R(\theta -t\pm \pi /2)E(\theta ), \qquad \theta -t\pm \pi /2>\pi /2,  \] truncated near $\theta =-t$. Here $\mathcal R$ is the Appendix A solution of \[  \tfrac 12\mathcal R^2-\theta +\arctan (\mathcal R'/\mathcal R)=0, \qquad \theta >\pi /2,  \] with $\mathcal R\downarrow 0$ as $\theta \downarrow \pi /2$. At a fixed point of the unrotated model the arms rotate counterclockwise with speed one. The cap center instead follows $R(t)E(-t)$, where $R(t)=\mathcal R(-2t)\sim 2\sqrt{-t}$, so it moves clockwise and inward. Its leading width is $\pi /R(t)$. The inset uses $X=e^{-tJ}[(R(t),0)+R(t)^{-1}(u,v)]$; its dashed reference is the leading grim reaper \[  G(p)=(-\arcsin (\tanh p),-\log \cosh p),\qquad p\in \mathbb R.  \] The orange curve includes the paper's normal correction $(-4t)^{-1}F(p)JG'(p)$, equations (2.19)–(2.21), and a smooth interpolation to the arms. These asymptotic formulas apply in the distant past; the figure's finite time interval carries no certified approximation-error bound.

text: B7D6B1E7217F Choose monotonically ordered heights $a_0<a_1<\cdots <a_ m$ and horizontal shifts $C_1,\ldots ,C_ m$. Angenent–You construct embedded eternal planar curve-shortening flows which for sufficiently negative time are assembled asymptotically from alternating grim reapers on consecutive strips. To record a definite nontrivial subfamily, take $m=3$. With $v_ k=\pi /(a_ k-a_{k-1})$, the separate asymptotic models are \[  x=C_ k+(-1)^ k\left[-v_ k^{-1}\log \sin (v_ k(y-a_{k-1}))+v_ kt\right], \qquad a_{k-1}<y<a_ k.  \] This formula describes the model translators, not the glued eternal solution. The actual flow is a graph $x=u(y,t)$ on $a_0<y<a_3$, exists for every $t\in \mathbb R$, and is complete, properly embedded and noncompact, with topology $\mathbb R$ and two ends asymptotic to the outer horizontal lines. The two-end and properness statements follow from this graphical description and the outer asymptotes. Curvature changes sign in the nontrivial chain; total absolute curvature is uniformly bounded. There is no closed formula or uniqueness assertion for $u$, and no entropy value is recorded. Source: [ AY18 ] , equation (3), Section 3.1 and Lemmas 3.8–3.10, pp. 2 and 8–13. The paper also constructs immersed ancient chains; those are not being labeled embedded by this selected case. The illustration uses $a_ k=k\pi $ and $C_ k=0$, so that the three model tips have horizontal velocities $-1,+1,-1$. It shows a numerical finite-start approximation: smoothly joined reapers at $t=-10$ are evolved by curve shortening, and slices from $t=-6$ to $t=9$ are displayed at the same spatial scale. The outer ends are truncated far outside the viewing window. The joins follow the construction in Section 3.2 and Figure 10, using the orientation of equation (3) and Figure 9. This computation is not a closed formula or a certified approximation of the eternal limit; the later shapes are numerical observations, not an additional asymptotic theorem.
